title: ConsumerConfig
description: The five consumer-side configuration knobs (RFC §10.5). The default requires no configuration; this exists only as the escape hatch, and it lives in the manifest the ecosystem already has (the `comprehendo` key in package.json, `[tool.comprehendo]` in pyproject.toml), never a new file format. Every knob is optional, so an empty object is a conforming config. Only the CONSUMER can override precedence: a provider gets no veto over a community corpus (RFC §10.4).

prefer.description: Per-package tier override, for when a native corpus is broken or stale. Keys are package names. Values are left as plain strings rather than an enum: RFC §10.5 shows only the `sidecar` value, and enumerating the tier vocabulary here would narrow the knob below what the RFC states.

pin.description: Per-corpus version pin, for reproducibility. Keys are corpus package names, values are version strings.

disable.description: Packages for which the consumer wants raw errors, please.

require.description: Per-package strictness, e.g. owner-endorsed corpus releases only (RFC §10.6). Keys are package names.

local.description: Mounts corpora for private packages, so an organization can make its internal libraries as fluent to agents as public ones without publishing anything. Keys are package names, values are paths.
